# Layered Architecture

Split the application into horizontal tiers where **each layer may only call the one below it**:
`api/` handles HTTP and nothing else, `service/` holds the domain rules and knows nothing about HTTP,
`repository/` talks to the database, `entity/` is the persistent shape. The constraint is the
architecture — without the "only downward" rule it is just four packages.

The payoff is substitution: swapping [[sqlite]] for [[h2-database]] between lab 2 and lab 3 touches
`repository/`, configuration and nothing else, because no controller ever held a query.

## As implemented

All three Java backends in [[information-systems-modelling]] use the **identical** split under
`pl.edu.pwr.tkubik.ism` — same packages, same artifactId, same names, across 11 → 41 → 76 Java files.
That repetition is not accidental; it is [[forward-copy-lab-progression]] preserving the skeleton
while each lab adds one capability to it.

| Lab | Java files | What the layering absorbed |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | 11 | generated API interfaces from [[contract-first-api-design]] |
| 3 | 41 | [[stateless-jwt-authentication]] added at the `config/` seam, not inside handlers |
| 4 | 76 | [[aspect-oriented-programming]], validation, uploads, dev/prod profiles |

Lab 4 is where the layering earns its keep. `GlobalExceptionHandler` converts anything thrown below
into an RFC 9457 `ProblemDetail` at the `api/` boundary, so no service needs to know it is being
called over HTTP, and no stack trace reaches a client. Aspects attach to pointcuts over the service
layer without any service method being edited.

## The observation that complicates it

Layering is a *static* decomposition. Everything this repo added after lab 2 that was genuinely
cross-cutting — logging, timing, statistics, security auditing — **could not be placed in a layer**,
which is precisely why lab 4 reaches for aspects. Layers handle the vertical slice; they have no
answer for the horizontal one. Recording both in the same codebase is what makes the pair legible.

## Limits observed

- **Zero tests exist for any service implementation.** The two integration tests in the repo drive
  the full stack end-to-end through MockMvc; nothing tests a layer in isolation, which is the usual
  argument for having layers at all. The testability benefit is claimed by structure, not
  demonstrated.
